concepts.why: Bilateral ventriculomegaly and ventricular enlargement are indicative of congenital hydrocephalus.
Bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns is a key feature of fetal ventriculomegaly.
Multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images are suggestive of intraventricular hemorrhage.
A roughened-appearing choroid plexus is consistent with a choroid plexus cyst.
Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion indicates normal fetal cerebral circulation.
Although the TORCH panel returned within normal limits, TORCH infection is a possible consideration in the differential diagnosis.
The comprehensive workup including coagulation studies returned within normal limits, but coagulopathy is a possible consideration in the differential diagnosis.
Bilateral ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls are indicative of a fetal brain anomaly.

rationales.F09: Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion suggests normal fetal cerebral circulation.
rationales.F12: A comprehensive workup with normal results rules out TORCH infection and coagulopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: Bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns, irregular ventricular walls, and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens support Congenital hydrocephalus, with no strong contradictions.
